# HALVORSEN & PRICE LLP — Counsel for Pinecrest Senior Living, Inc.
September 29, 2026 · Via email

Re: Your demand dated [session 1] — Juniper Health Staffing / Pinecrest

Counsel:

We represent Pinecrest. Your demand letter asserts (i) $340,000 in unpaid invoices, (ii) $112,000 in conversion fees for seven employees, and (iii) a "tortious interference" claim valued at $410,000. We respond briefly.

1. **Interference.** Pinecrest cannot "interfere" with a contract to which it is a party, and in any event Juniper **consented** to the hires. Your own account manager wrote on February 11, 2026: *"consider the fee waived … as a one-off, you guys have been a great partner. Just keep the RN orders coming."* (copy attached). Your letter states that Juniper "never consented to any direct hire." That statement is contradicted by Juniper's own records. We enclose a draft Rule 12(b)(6) motion directed to the interference count that we will file if you sue on it.
2. **Conversion fees.** Section 3 permits Juniper to waive the fee; it did so. To the extent you contend the waiver covered only two individuals, that is a contract dispute, not a tort.
3. **Invoices.** Pinecrest disputes J-4533 (padded hours; notice given within 15 days) and will pay the undisputed balance of the remaining invoices upon resolution of the conversion-fee issue. Pinecrest reserves all rights.
4. We note your letter threatens suit in the Superior Court. We trust you have reviewed the parties' agreement in full.

Very truly yours, /s/ R. Halvorsen
# DRAFT — DEFENDANT'S MOTION TO DISMISS COUNT III (TORTIOUS INTERFERENCE) UNDER RULE 12(b)(6)
…A party to a contract cannot be liable for tortiously interfering with its own contract (*Ashby v. Caldera Partners*, 212 Col. App. 3d 440 (2019)). Nor can a claim lie for interference with Juniper's at-will relationships with its own nurses where Pinecrest acted with Juniper's express consent (Feb. 11 email, Ex. 1) and for a legitimate business purpose (corporate directive to reduce agency spend, Ex. 2) — justification is a complete defense (*Restatement (Second) of Torts §§766, 767, 773*)…
# Session 1 assessment — Juniper / Pinecrest

**As of October 26, 2026, updated with the client's follow-up.** This is a preliminary assessment on the client file. The demand letter is a draft for client review. The current record does not support demanding $862,000 or filing a merits lawsuit.

## What the agreement requires

The January 15, 2024 signed staffing agreement requires payment of hourly invoices within 30 days, interest on late amounts at 1% per month, and notice of an invoice dispute within 15 days of receipt. An invoice not disputed within that period is deemed accepted. A direct hire of personnel Juniper introduced triggers a conversion fee of 25% of that person's first-year annualized compensation unless Juniper waives it in writing. Either party may terminate on 60 days' notice. Consequential damages are excluded, while liability for unpaid fees and conversion fees is not capped.

Exhibit C requires **exclusive AAA binding arbitration before one arbitrator in Capital City, Columbia**, for disputes relating to the agreement, including arbitrability. Its only stated merits-court exception is a claim **solely** to collect an undisputed invoice under $25,000 in small-claims court; none of these invoices qualifies. A court may hear provisional injunctive relief in aid of arbitration. The prevailing party can recover reasonable attorney fees and costs in arbitration and in an action to compel arbitration. Filing a merits suit risks a stay, an order to arbitrate, and Pinecrest's fees for compelling arbitration. The FAA provisions in the library support enforcement of a written arbitration clause in a transaction involving commerce; that commerce predicate has not yet been documented in this file. The delegation of arbitrability is explicit in Exhibit C. [FAA §§2–4](../../library/faa_2_4.md); [fee-shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).

## Claims and value

| Item | Present record | Assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| Five unpaid invoices | Original total: $68,400 + $71,250 + $66,100 + $74,800 + $59,450 = **$340,000**. Juniper's CEO now confirms **about $3,100** of June shifts were double-entered. Using $3,100 provisionally gives **about $336,900** corrected total and **about $71,700** for J-4533. | Four invoices without recorded dispute total **$340,000 − $74,800 = $265,200**. The June invoice, J-4533, faces a July 9 objection. Juniper must credit the actual double-billed amount, still to be established. The CEO says the rest is legitimate, but no shift records are available to test that assertion. The record lacks J-4533's receipt date, so whether the objection met the 15-day deadline cannot be decided. July shifts also lack supporting requests or time records. |
| Seven direct hires | CEO estimate: 7 × 25% × $64,000 = **$112,000** | **Rosa and Tay were expressly waived in Bell's February 11 written email.** Do not charge their conversion fees. Five hires remain potentially chargeable: Priya, Luis, Keisha, Anne, and Victor. At $64,000 *each*, the illustration is 5 × 25% × $64,000 = **$80,000**, but the seven-person average does not establish these five actual salaries. Seek compensation and introduction records before stating a fixed fee. |
| Lost profits / tortious interference | **$410,000** asserted for 12 months | No supported tort claim on this record. Pinecrest is a party to the staffing contract and cannot interfere with its own contract. The May 2 email cites a corporate mandate to reduce agency use, rather than improper interference. No third-party contract or expectancy, improper means, or profit calculation is documented. The agreement also bars consequential damages. Do not include this amount in a demand. [Tortious interference](../../library/columbia_tortious_interference.md). |

The CEO's original arithmetic reconciles as **$340,000 + $112,000 + $410,000 = $862,000**. Using the **approximate** $3,100 billing error and illustrative $32,000 attributed to two waived hires, and removing the unsupported $410,000 tort figure, gives **about $416,900 = $862,000 − $3,100 − $32,000 − $410,000**. This is only an illustration, equal to **about $336,900 corrected invoices + $80,000 assumed conversion fees**. It is not a proved or final amount: the approximately $71,700 June balance remains disputed and the five individual compensation figures are unknown. A more defensible currently quantified invoice base is **$265,200**. Contract interest may add value, but the file does not give invoice receipt dates, payment history beyond the open-invoice list, or a calculation convention for partial months; no interest figure is asserted yet.

## Strengths, defenses, and risks

The signed agreement, itemized invoice list, and Bell's July 20 identification of seven hires support contract claims. Pinecrest's July 9 objection is specific to J-4533; the other four are recorded without dispute notices. Unobjected invoices are prima facie evidence of debt under the library's account-stated rule, subject to proof of receipt and the actual course of dealing. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).

Bell's February 11 email says the fee is waived for Rosa and Tay **“as a one-off.”** Bell now confirms he waived only those two and did not agree to waive fees for the other five. That supports Juniper's position but does not resolve Pinecrest's possible reliance argument. The April 22 “same deal as before?” text and Bell's “ha, we'll talk,” plus the May 14 text, “call me,” and six-minute call concerning Luis and Keisha, create a factual risk of further implied waiver or estoppel; they do not show an express written waiver for the other five. The call's exact contents and Pinecrest's understanding remain unknown. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md). Alleging all seven conversion fees, concealing the February waiver, or ignoring the June overcharge would be unsound; counsel must communicate adverse facts and avoid unsupported claims. [Fee-shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).

The May 2 staffing email says Pinecrest would reduce agency use and finish current requests. It does not establish a contract breach or an effective 60-day termination notice by itself. No minimum purchase obligation appears in the agreement. Lost future orders and lost-profit causation are therefore especially weak. We should pursue invoices and supportable conversion fees in negotiation, then arbitration if necessary, while recognizing the prevailing-party fee exposure on unsuccessful claims.

## Immediate evidence needed

The client has no additional records or information for the unanswered questions. The invoice receipt dates, any further objections or payments, J-4533 shift records, July staffing requests and time records, individual compensation and introduction proof for the five hires, and the May 14 call's exact contents remain unknown. Seek relevant records from Pinecrest during negotiation or arbitration and preserve those Juniper can locate later. No court filing should be prepared from the $862,000 spreadsheet.
# Draft demand letter — for client review

**October 26, 2026**

**Via email**  
Hanna Lindqvist  
Pinecrest Senior Living, Inc.

**Re: Juniper Health Staffing, LLC — unpaid invoices and conversion fees**

Dear Ms. Lindqvist:

I represent Juniper Health Staffing, LLC concerning Pinecrest's obligations under the January 15, 2024 Staffing Services Agreement. Juniper's original records show five unpaid invoices totaling **$340,000**:

| Invoice | Amount |
|---|---:|
| J-4411 | $68,400 |
| J-4452 | $71,250 |
| J-4490 | $66,100 |
| J-4533 | $74,800 |
| J-4571 | $59,450 |
| **Total** | **$340,000** |

Juniper received your July 9 email disputing hours on J-4533. Juniper has since identified **about $3,100 in double-entered June shifts** and will credit the exact amount once confirmed. Using $3,100 provisionally, the J-4533 balance is **about $71,700** ($74,800 − $3,100), and the five-invoice balance is **about $336,900** ($340,000 − $3,100). Please provide the other shifts and hours you challenge and the audit materials supporting your position; Juniper will review them promptly. The other four invoices total **$265,200** ($340,000 − $74,800); our records show no dispute notice for those invoices. Please remit that amount now and identify any payment or objection that our records do not reflect. Juniper seeks the supported balance of J-4533 and contractual late interest, subject to review of the June audit.

The agreement also requires a conversion fee of 25% of first-year annualized compensation for personnel Juniper introduced and Pinecrest hired. Juniper's records identify five hires for which it has no written fee waiver: **Priya S., Luis F., Keisha B., Anne O., and Victor H.** Please provide each hire's start date and first-year annualized compensation within 14 days so the contractual fees can be calculated and paid. Juniper's February 11 written waiver covered **Rosa M. and Tay W.** only; this letter makes no demand for fees for those two employees. If Pinecrest contends that any other fee was waived, please identify the communication and circumstances on which it relies.

Please respond by **November 9, 2026**, with payment of the $265,200 invoice balance for which we have no recorded objection, the requested information, and a proposal to resolve the remaining amounts. Payment instructions can be coordinated through counsel. Juniper remains willing to resolve the entire matter promptly. If it cannot be resolved, Juniper reserves its right to pursue the supported claims through the arbitration process in Exhibit C, including contractual interest and applicable attorney fees and costs.

Sincerely,

Counsel for Juniper Health Staffing, LLC

---

**Drafting note to client (remove before sending):** This letter deliberately does not claim the CEO's $862,000. The $410,000 lost-profit/tort item lacks a supported basis; Rosa and Tay's conversion fees were waived; Juniper admits an approximately $3,100 June billing error; and the five remaining fees require individual compensation figures. Receipt dates, underlying shift records, and hire records remain unavailable. The letter has not been sent.
